# JpegEncoderOptions

[DotGame.Imaging](README.md) · `DotGame.Imaging.Jpeg` · class

```csharp
public sealed class JpegEncoderOptions
```

How [`JpegCodec.Encode`](JpegCodec.md#encode) writes an image: its defaults are cjpeg 3.2.1's, and with the same settings the file is byte for byte what cjpeg writes. Each setting is the cjpeg switch it names.

## Remarks

A setting out of its range isn't caught when it's set: [`JpegCodec.Encode`](JpegCodec.md#encode) throws `System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for it.

## Properties

### Grayscale

```csharp
public bool Grayscale { get; init; }
```

Whether the file is grayscale, its one component the pixels' luma (`-grayscale`).

### OptimizeHuffman

```csharp
public bool OptimizeHuffman { get; init; }
```

Whether the Huffman tables are made for the image, in a pass that counts its symbols, rather than the standard ones (`-optimize`). A progressive file always has them.

### Progressive

```csharp
public bool Progressive { get; init; }
```

Whether the file is progressive, with libjpeg's simple progression (`-progressive`).

### Quality

```csharp
public int Quality { get; init; }
```

The quality, 0 to 100 (`-quality`; 75 by default), scaling the standard quantization tables as libjpeg does: below 50 by 5000 / quality, from 50 by 200 - 2 x quality (0 counts as 1).

### Subsampling

```csharp
public JpegSubsampling Subsampling { get; init; }
```

Types: [`JpegSubsampling`](JpegSubsampling.md)

The chroma subsampling (`-sample`): 4:2:0 by default. A grayscale file has none.
